A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLMM survey despite changes to the title and authorship. Their text, figures, tables, and references support comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 adds Appendix A on publication venues, which is included in this assessment.

before.justification: v1 reports original descriptive analysis of the surveyed literature, including recovery-method proportions in Section 2.5.2 and missing-modality evaluation and training statistics in Section 3.7.

after.justification: v3 retains the authors' literature statistics in Sections 5.3 and 6 and adds annual publication counts in Figure 1a. These are original data-analysis results, although neither version reports original model experiments.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an executable MLMM algorithm or model. The revised taxonomy and expanded descriptions of existing approaches do not establish changes to an authors-proposed method.

E1.justification: The application domains and Table 3 dataset catalog are retained. Neither version adds an executed training task or benchmark evaluation; changes to surveyed examples do not establish new evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Both compare surveyed methods descriptively and acknowledge that heterogeneous settings prevent standardized performance comparisons. Neither reports an evaluated comparator set against an authors-proposed model.

E3.justification: The stated literature-collection cutoff changes from September to October 2024, while the starting year remains 2012 and the claimed corpus remains 315 papers. This is a limited reported collection-setting revision; the PDFs do not establish whether the retained percentage analyses were recomputed.

E4.justification: Figure 1a adds a descriptive analysis of publication volume over 2014–October 2024. The earlier method-frequency and missing-modality-setting analyses remain, and no model ablations or robustness experiments are added.

E5.justification: Both versions use descriptive counts and percentages. Neither adds repeated-run or seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v3 adds annual publication-count results in Figure 1a and changes the non-recovery share from 24.6% in v1 Section 2.5.2 to 24.5% in v3 Section 5.3. The other principal literature proportions, including 38%/62% and 36.4%/63.6%, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theoretical results or proofs. Expanded explanations of existing regularization, correlation, and attention methods do not introduce new derivations; changing the modality-count notation from H to N is equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The central taxonomy contribution is refined from four dimensions and thirteen categories to two aspects, four types, and twelve categories, grouping regularization and correlation under coordinated representation. The first-comprehensive-survey claim and overall cross-domain remit remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses generation artifacts and hallucinations, expands the existing benchmarking agenda with a MultiBench-style proposal, and clarifies distillation exceptions for incomplete training data. Some narrower cautions, including the time-series-only validation of regularization methods, are omitted.

D1.justification: The Paper Collection paragraph now identifies specific conferences and journals and includes 'multi-view learning' among example search terms. New Appendix A expands the venue abbreviations. These additions document literature collection more specifically, without supplying a reproducible corpus or new implementation resources.

R1.justification: Selected literature is updated: v3 adds Fuyu, OtterHD, MultiBench, and additional correlation-method references, while removing examples including Qwen-VL, AnyMAL, and HeMIS. This changes the supporting literature without substantially changing the survey's research positioning.

P1.justification: Substantial rewriting spans the introduction, method explanations, applications, and future directions. The former Methodology section becomes separate taxonomy-overview, data-processing, strategy-design, and discussion sections, with renamed categories and clearer internal subdivisions. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1a replaces the multimodal-input illustration with a publication chart. Figure 2 and Table 1 are restructured for the revised taxonomy, and Figure 6 and several captions are updated. Most of the seventeen figures, three tables, and single-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: The explicit taxonomy overview and reorganized explanations make the survey easier to navigate, while the generation-risk discussion and more concrete benchmarking agenda add useful guidance. These benefits outweigh the limited pruning of examples and cautions. Most evidence remains unchanged, and the cross-study comparability limitation acknowledged in both versions remains unresolved.
